description: Free, open-source 2D skeletal animation editor with a native Defold runtime for meshes, IK, physics, constraints, skins, events, and animation blending.
name: Rigby2D

releases.message:
Rigby2D 0.6.1 builds on Mammoth with the fixes and requests from its first days: **hide and lock parts** while you work, a **Tree that reads like a hierarchy**, **weights you can read on hover**, **panels that stay on top**, physics that **settles before the first frame** of a render, **15 new AI assistant tools**, and a new **SDL3 runtime** (preview). If you have 0.6.0, the editor offers this update by itself.

## What's new

### Working on the rig

- **Show and lock**: every bone and slot row in the Tree has an eye and a lock. Hide parts in the viewport to work on what's behind them, and lock parts so clicks and box selections go past them. <kbd>Alt</kbd>+click does a whole branch, and *View ▸ Show and unlock all* resets everything. Editor-only: renders, exports and the runtimes always show everything.
- **Branch guides** in the Tree: lines join each bone to its children down open branches, so deep rigs stay readable.
- **Collapse all and expand all** bones in the Tree. (#45, thanks @greeenos)
- **Vertex weights on hover**: in Weights mode, the vertex under the cursor shows each bone's influence in %.
- **View ▸ Bone links**: dashed lines from bones to their parents, for the selected branch (the default), all bones, or off.
- **Pinned panels**: a pin on popped-out panel windows (desktop app) keeps them on top of every other app.
- **Slot tint keys**: the slot tint can now be keyed in Animate mode. (#43, thanks @h897105167)

### Animation and rendering

- **Physics settles before the first frame**: hair, tails and cloth already hang at rest when a render starts, instead of dropping into place on frame 1. Rigs without physics render exactly as before.
- **Faster dopesheet drawing** on large animations. (#44, thanks @greeenos)

### AI assistants (MCP): 45 → 60 tools

- **Film effects**: `set_film_effects`, `set_layer_effects` and `set_emitter` (snow, rain, dust, sparks); `inspect_project` lists the effects.
- **Rigging and animation**: constraint keys and world-space IK target keys, skins and attachment copies, meshes from the image outline or a grid, automatic, manual and smoothed weights, physics baked into keys, and an animation checker (`lint_animations`) that finds jumps, loop seams and missing images.

### Runtimes

- **SDL3** (preview): play Rigby2D animations in C++ games on SDL3's 2D renderer, with the Defold runtime's golden-tested core. A CMake project with an example player; PNG atlas pages load without extra libraries on SDL 3.4.
- **PixiJS on npm**: `npm install @rigby2d/pixi-js`, now in TypeScript. (#41, thanks @BlackRam-oss)
- **Community runtimes**: [RigAxis](https://github.com/zrurf/RigAxis) by zrurf brings Rigby2D to Unreal Engine 5, now listed in the docs.

## Fixes

- Spine skeletons whose curves came from a placeholder version (like Spineboy) no longer spin their legs. (#40, thanks @unreal79)
- Every label follows a change of interface language at once, without a restart. (#42, thanks @h897105167)
- The Graph editor's curve preset menu opens again.
- Number fields in dialogs show the keyboard focus ring.
- Tree and timeline fixes.

Rigby2D 0.6 Mammoth is our biggest release yet: **a new interface built on one design language**, **dockable panels with tabs**, **film effects**, **2.5D turns and warp deformers**, rigging tools that keep up with you, **Aseprite import**, a **command-line tool** and a **Ren'Py runtime**. If you have 0.5, the editor offers this update by itself.

## What's new

### A new interface

Every panel, dialog, toolbar and label was rebuilt on one design system.

- **One look everywhere**: shared colours, spacing and type, and one set of buttons, toggles, fields and dialogs. Escape and clicking outside close every dialog the same way.
- **Real icons**: one SVG icon set (Lucide) across the toolbars, timeline, tree and inspector. No emoji.
- **Tree and inspector rebuilt**, with shorter, consistent wording and proper plurals.
- **Themes**: Rigby Dark, **Mammoth** and Rigby Light, or make your own and share it as a `.rigbytheme` file (*View ▸ Themes…*). The colour picker and every control follow the theme.
- **Checked automatically**: every main view and 15 dialogs at three window sizes, in English and Chinese, with keyboard focus that stays inside dialogs.

### Your layout

- **Dock any panel**: drag it by its tab to the left, right or bottom, or into another panel's tabs.
- **Saved layouts**, in the browser editor too: *View ▸ Layouts* keeps where panels sit and how wide they are (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>1</kbd>–<kbd>9</kbd>).
- **Rig panel**: skins, constraints by type, meshes and events in one place, so the tree keeps just bones, draw order, animations and images.
- A tighter first layout that gives the viewport more room.

### Film effects

For short films and cutscenes, in the Film workspace:

- **Layer effects** on any bone or slot: drop shadow, light shading with a rim light, glow, blur and colour grade.
- **Particles**: snow, dust, sparks and rain from emitters on bones, deterministic so every render matches the preview.
- **Motion blur** and **depth of field** in renders, and a colour grade for the whole shot.
- Live in the viewport and in every render path, on the GPU. Game exports never see them.

### 2.5D turn and warp deformers

- **Make turnable**: select a head's parts and one control bone turns and tilts it in depth. It plays in every runtime, and games can drive it live.
- **Shape a side by hand**: fix any turn angle with a lattice, and the in-between angles blend.
- **Warp deformers**: nested lattices over meshes, keyable, and resizable without losing their keys. Baked to mesh deform keys, so every runtime plays them.
- Additive slider constraints now work in every runtime, so Spine files that use them play correctly.

### Rigging that keeps up with you

- **Test pose while painting weights**: <kbd>Alt</kbd>+drag any bone and keep painting on the posed mesh. **Wiggle** swings the bone while you paint.
- **Weights button** on the toolbar: one click from a mesh to painting its weights.
- **Bone only**: in Setup mode, move, turn or scale a bone and its children and images stay where they are drawn, IK chains included.
- **Transform constraints that never jump**, a clear Driver and Driven, offsets set by moving the bone, and pick buttons to choose bones by clicking.
- **Point bones** (#37): bones with no length, for pivots and anchors.
- **Better mesh generation** (#38): locked vertices, every shape in an image, holes, and a minimum angle.
- **Find** in the tree and **drag to reparent**.
- **Tween lines** in the dopesheet show where values blend between keys.

### Pipeline

- **Aseprite import**: `.aseprite` and `.ase` files open directly. Layers become parts, tags become animations at Aseprite's timing, hidden layers become variant animations, and blend modes are kept.
- **`rigby` on the command line**: inspect, validate, convert, export, AutoRig, run Python scripts, call any MCP tool, and render on the GPU, for scripts and CI ([docs](https://rigby2d.com/docs/cli.html)).
- **Ren'Py runtime**, the ninth: characters with expressions, lip-sync from voice lines, blinks, gaze and 2.5D turns in visual novels. Pure Python, golden-tested against the core. Runtime and demo zips are attached below.
- **MCP**: add, edit and delete constraints without the editor (45 tools).

### Also new

- **The Mammoth demo** (*File ▸ Open demo*): the star of 0.6, with its walk, its trumpet call and film effects.
- **A new splash screen** with a Start button. Turn its animation off in *Preferences ▸ General*.
- **A new What's new tour** for 0.6.

### Fixes

- Spine 4.3 `.skel` files with local, additive or clamped transform constraints open, and exports keep those options.
- Shortcuts work on Russian and other non-Latin keyboard layouts.
- The tree lists a bone's parts front first, like the draw order.
- Pixel art turns the pixel grid on by itself on import.
- Layer sets picked on the desktop keep their names and order.

### Thanks

0.6 was shaped by our community: **Geokima** (the interface review, docking and the rigging workflow), **Skadii** (the Rig panel, tween lines, the Weights button and saved layouts) and **MysterHen** (point bones and mesh generation). Thank you.

Everything from 0.5.1 is included: the PixiJS runtime, Defold models in the editor and the editor in Simplified Chinese.

Rigby2D 0.5.1: a **PixiJS runtime**, **Rigby2D models that play live in the Defold editor**, the editor **fully in Simplified Chinese**, and a long list of animator requests from our community. If you have 0.5.0, the editor offers this update by itself.

## What's new

### PixiJS runtime

Rigby2D characters now play natively in **PixiJS 8**, on WebGL and WebGPU ([guide](https://github.com/jaisurya-dev-art/rigby2d/blob/main/runtimes/pixi/README.md)).

- A skeleton is an ordinary PixiJS `Container`: filters, masks, tint, blend modes, bounds and pointer events all work, and it batches with your sprites.
- Everything plays, exactly as in the editor: meshes and weights, IK, transform, path, physics and slider constraints, clipping, skins, two-color tint, events, and layered tracks with crossfades and queues.
- **Optional WebAssembly core**: the Rust runtime compiled to WASM (about 150 KB gzipped), about twice as fast as the JavaScript path for crowds.

### Defold: Rigby2D models, live in the editor

A new **Rigby2D Model** component (`.rigbymodel`), like a sprite or a Spine model: add it to a game object and the Defold editor plays it in the scene view. Pick the animation and skin in the Properties panel and press Space to watch it move ([guide](https://github.com/jaisurya-dev-art/rigby2d/blob/main/runtimes/defold/README.md#rigby2d-models-live-in-the-editor)).

- **One-click export**: *File ▸ Export ▸ Defold model…* writes the skeleton, the images with a Defold atlas, the component and a ready game object into your Defold project.
- **Drawn natively** in the game, driven by `rigby.play`, `rigby.queue`, `rigby.on_event`, `rigby.bone` and `go.get` / `go.set`.
- Uses a regular Defold atlas, so texture profiles and compression apply. The editor plugin runs on Windows, macOS and Linux.
- Also from the AI assistant: the `export_defold_model` MCP tool.

### Simplified Chinese

The whole editor interface is now in Simplified Chinese (*Preferences ▸ General ▸ Language*).

### Animating

- **Setup and Animate tabs** in the menu bar; the timeline hides in Setup to give the viewport room.
- **Timeline bar**: frame rate, playback speed and timecode where you look, and **boomerang** playback (to the end and back).
- **Zoom the timeline**: <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+wheel zooms time around the cursor, <kbd>Alt</kbd>+wheel pans.
- **Cut, copy and paste keys** from the right-click menu, with *Paste here* at the frame you clicked.
- **Curve of new keys**: start new keys linear, eased or stepped (*Preferences ▸ Editing*).

### Rigging and the viewport

- **Bone colors**: give bones their own color to tell limbs and sides apart.
- **Hold Shift while translating** to move along one axis.
- **Show or hide each overlay**: bones, clipping masks, bounding boxes, paths, points, or all at once.
- **Pixel grid** for pixel art, with the grid on pixel edges.
- **Undo, redo, fit and show-bones buttons** next to the mode tabs, and <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd> to show or hide bones.
- **Slots fold** in the tree, showing only the visible image, so busy rigs stay readable.
- **AutoRig imports PNGs** straight from its dialog.

### Also new

- **Open files from your desktop**: double-click a `.rigby` file, or drop files on the window (#35).
- **Tooltips show shortcuts** in the keys of your keymap.
- **Interface scale** is a slider from 75% to 200%.
- The editor window opens maximized; the renderer and shortcut presets live in *Preferences*.
- **Help menu** with a Support dialog, and our community is now on [Discord](https://discord.gg/PGgaTwbNH).

### Fixes

- **Stretching two-bone IK** reaches its target when the chain is bent (every runtime).
- **Weight painting keeps a mesh's deform keys** (#36).
- **Image sequences** read their base name, start and digits from the image (`guy-01` gives `guy-01`, `guy-02`…).
- **Child bones** added from a bone keep its length instead of shrinking.
- The desktop app no longer shows the browser's right-click menu (#34).

Everything from 0.5.0 is included: the Defold runtime, sprite sheet export, SVG import, mesh from image and the production-ready Godot runtime.

Rigby2D 0.5: our biggest update yet. A **native Defold runtime**, **sprite sheet export** drawn on the GPU, **SVG import** from Inkscape and Affinity, **generate a mesh from an image** in one click, and the **Godot runtime, production-ready**. If you have 0.4.x, the editor offers this update by itself.

## What's new

### Defold runtime

Rigby2D now runs in Defold: a native C++ runtime, on every platform Defold ships to (Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS, HTML5), matching the editor frame by frame ([guide](https://github.com/jaisurya-dev-art/rigby2d/blob/main/runtimes/defold/README.md)).

- **Add it as a library**: in *game.project ▸ Project ▸ Dependencies*, add `https://github.com/jaisurya-dev-art/rigby2d/releases/latest/download/rigby2d-defold.zip` and choose *Project ▸ Fetch Libraries*.
- **Everything plays**: meshes and weights, IK and physics, skins, events, tracks with crossfades, and Rigby2D scenes.
- Checked in CI against the reference runtime on every push.

### Sprite sheet export

*File ▸ Export ▸ Sprite sheet…* turns any animation into frames for engines and tools that play frames instead of bones.

- **Three formats**: a packed sheet with JSON (Phaser, PixiJS, TexturePacker, Aseprite tags), a Defold atlas with its frames, or PNG frames.
- **Drawn on the GPU**: 120 large frames in about 4 seconds instead of about 30.
- **Big sheets split** across several sheets within the size you choose, with JSON that Phaser and PixiJS load as one. The dialog shows the frame size and sheet count before you export, and the largest size that fits on one sheet. Power-of-two sheet sizes are an option.
- Also from the AI assistant: the `export_sprite_sheet` MCP tool.

### SVG import

*File ▸ Import ▸ SVG…* brings in a drawing from Inkscape, Affinity or Illustrator like a PSD: every layer becomes a part, placed where it was drawn, ready for AutoRig. Inkscape sublayers are parts of their own, hidden layers come in hidden, and you choose the size it's drawn at.

### Generate mesh from image

One click turns an image into a mesh: Rigby2D traces the art, places the points and builds the triangles, keeping corners sharp. Then bend it.

### Godot runtime, production-ready

RigbySkeleton2D and RigbyScene2D are complete and out of preview, tested against the editor on every frame.

### Also new

- **Your own shortcuts**: rebind any action, keep more than one key for it, and export or import your keymap. The default preset is now called *Spine-like*.
- **Copy and paste keys** in the timeline, across bones and frames, with several regions at once and three paste modes.
- **Layered PNGs in place**: same-size PNGs exported from a drawing land where they were drawn, like PSD layers, ready for AutoRig. AutoRig's spine now finds the neck and head.
- **Opening projects in the browser editor**: an ordinary file picker, or drop the files on the window. Rigby2D finds the project among them and asks only for any file that's missing.
- **Every export and render reports back** in a dialog: where the files went (with *Show in folder* on desktop) or what went wrong. Playback pauses while they run.
- **Phaser 4**: the Phaser runtime runs on Phaser 3.60+ and 4.
- **What's new in 0.5**: a short tour on the first start, also in *Help ▸ What's new*.
- **Support Rigby2D**: a [funding page](https://rigby2d.com/fund/) and *Help ▸ Supporters*.

### Fixes

- Moving a mesh to another bone no longer crashes (#22, #28).
- Bone hover skips bones without a world transform (#25).
- DragonBones import opens the character, not a weapon or bullet listed first.
- The physics section says that physics simulates during playback (#27).
- Auto-save and add-ons work on Linux, where the app data folder was refused (#29).

Everything from 0.4.3 is included: the Cocos Creator runtime and DragonBones projects that match the original.
